\textbf{Source.} Tadelis (2013), \emph{Game Theory: An Introduction}, Exercise 5.3 ``Nash and IESDS'', pp.~95--96 {[}PDF p.~114--115{]}. Answer in the source: none (the preface, p.~xiii, says about half of the exercises are solved on Princeton UP's website). Reproduced verbatim.

\begin{quote}
\textbf{Nash and IESDS:} Consider a two-player game with \(m\) pure strategies for each player that can be represented by an \(m \times m\) matrix.

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\alph{enumi}.}
\item
  Show that if \(m = 2\) and the game has a unique pure-strategy Nash equilibrium then this is the unique strategy profile that survives IESDS.
\item
  Show that if \(m = 3\) and the game has a unique pure-strategy equilibrium then it may not be the only strategy profile that survives IESDS.
\end{enumerate}
\end{quote}
